quiz_exm1:1.q: Every label has been removed from this lecture drawing of a microscope. What does the lecture say focuses its beam?
quiz_exm1:1.r: A specimen holder halfway down the column and a fluorescent screen and film at the bottom mark the transmission electron microscope, in which magnets focus a beam of electrons (p. 92). Glass lenses focus light in the light microscope (p. 91).
quiz_exm1:1.alt: Cutaway drawing of a tall column with a beam passing down through several ring-shaped parts to a flat plate at the bottom; a round inset shows a mesh

quiz_exm1:10.q: A microscope uses glass lenses to focus light. What is the highest magnification the lecture gives for it?
quiz_exm1:10.r: Light microscope: magnification up to 1,500 times (p. 91). SEM: up to 100,000 times (p. 93). TEM: up to 500,000 times (p. 92).

quiz_exm1:11.q: Which order runs from the lowest to the highest top magnification given in the lecture?
quiz_exm1:11.r: Light microscope 1,500 times (p. 91), scanning electron microscope 100,000 times (p. 93), transmission electron microscope 500,000 times (p. 92).

quiz_exm1:12.q: This colour image of kidney tubules is one of three views of the same tissue in the lecture. Which instrument produced it?
quiz_exm1:12.r: A stained colour section is light microscopy (p. 94). The lecture then shows the same tubules as a grey thin section by TEM (p. 95, p. 120) and as a 3-D surface by SEM (p. 96).
quiz_exm1:12.alt: Pink-stained section of several tubules cut across, with dark nuclei and the letters C, D and P

quiz_exm1:13.q: This grey image shows a thin slice through a kidney tubule with detail inside the cells. With what were sections like this stained, according to the lecture?
o: Gold from a sputter coating unit
quiz_exm1:13.r: A grey thin section with internal cell detail is transmission electron microscopy (TEM: kidney tubules, p. 120). Ultrathin sections are stained with lead citrate and uranyl acetate (p. 117). Gold coating is for SEM (p. 126).
quiz_exm1:13.alt: Grey micrograph of a ring of cells around an open space, with a fringe on the inner surface, blue arrows and the letter P

quiz_exm1:14.q: This image gives a surface view of a broken-open kidney tubule. With what was the specimen coated before viewing, according to the lecture?
quiz_exm1:14.r: A 3-D surface view is scanning electron microscopy (p. 96). SEM specimens are fixed, dehydrated, critical point dried and coated in a sputter coating unit with gold (pp. 124-126).
quiz_exm1:14.alt: Grey micrograph showing the surface of a broken-open tube in relief, with the letter P

quiz_exm1:15.q: The lecture photographs the specimen supports for its three microscopes side by side. Which instrument takes the tiny support at the arrow?
quiz_exm1:15.r: The smallest support, on the right, is the TEM grid; the glass slide in the middle is for the light microscope and the metal stubs on the left are for the SEM (p. 101, p. 118, p. 127).
quiz_exm1:15.alt: Photograph of three columns of specimen holders on a pale background, with a coin for scale; a yellow arrow points to a very small holder on the right

quiz_exm1:16.q: Which instrument takes the specimen at the arrow, which is mounted on a metal stub beside a coin for scale?
quiz_exm1:16.r: The left column of the photograph, with whole specimens on metal stubs, is labelled SEM; the glass slide is LM and the tiny grid is TEM (p. 101, p. 127).
quiz_exm1:16.alt: Photograph of three columns of specimen holders on a pale background, with a coin for scale; a yellow arrow points to a round holder on the left

quiz_exm1:17.q: Which pairing of embedding medium and microscope matches the lecture?
o: Epon for LM, paraffin for TEM
Paraffin for LM, gold for TEM
Gold for LM, Epon for TEM
Epon for LM, gold for SEM
Paraffin for LM, Epon for TEM
quiz_exm1:17.r: Embedding is in paraffin for light microscopy (p. 98) and in Epon for TEM (p. 110). Gold is the sputter coating for SEM (p. 126).

quiz_exm1:18.q: Which fixative appears on the lecture's list for TEM but not on its list for light microscopy?
quiz_exm1:18.r: Light microscopy: fixation in formalin (p. 97). TEM: formalin, glutaraldehyde and osmium tetroxide (p. 109). Xylene and ethanol are dehydration agents and uranyl acetate is a stain for ultrathin sections (p. 117).

quiz_exm1:19.q: On the lecture's preparation slides, xylene is listed in the dehydration step for which specimens?
quiz_exm1:19.r: Light microscopy: dehydration with ethanol and xylene (p. 97). TEM and SEM list ethanol only (p. 109, p. 124).

quiz_exm1:2.q: Every label has been removed from this lecture drawing. Which microscope is it, and what top magnification does the lecture give for it?
quiz_exm1:2.r: The specimen sits at the bottom of the column, with a scanner, a detector beside the specimen and a monitor: the scanning electron microscope, magnification up to 100,000 times (p. 93). The TEM reaches 500,000 times (p. 92) and the light microscope 1,500 times (p. 91).
quiz_exm1:2.alt: Cutaway drawing of a tall column with a beam passing down to a small disc at the bottom, with a box beside the disc wired to a screen showing an insect

quiz_exm1:20.q: Which step of preparation for light microscopy is this instrument used for?
quiz_exm1:20.r: The instrument is a microtome, used for sectioning the paraffin block (p. 99). The order is fixation and dehydration, embedding, sectioning, then mounting and staining (pp. 97-100).
quiz_exm1:20.alt: Photograph of a person turning the wheel of a bench instrument that holds a small block against a blade

quiz_exm1:21.q: Ultrathin sections for the TEM are being cut in this photograph. What is the knife made of, according to the lecture?
quiz_exm1:21.r: Ultrathin sections are cut with a diamond knife (p. 114). Copper is the grid, gold is the SEM coating and paraffin is the embedding medium for light microscopy.
quiz_exm1:21.alt: Close-up photograph of a small block held in a chuck next to a blade with a trough

quiz_exm1:22.q: These ultrathin sections are floating in a boat of water. On what are sections like these carried into the TEM, according to the lecture's drawing?
quiz_exm1:22.r: The TEM drawing shows a 3 mm copper grid with three sections on the specimen holder (p. 92), and the lecture shows the section supports used in electron microscopy (p. 116). Glass slides are for LM and stubs for SEM (p. 101).
quiz_exm1:22.alt: Photograph of many small pale rectangles floating on a dark red liquid surface

quiz_exm1:23.q: For which technique is the unit in this photograph used, according to the lecture?
quiz_exm1:23.r: This is the Balzers unit used for freeze-fracturing (p. 121), which exposes the E and P faces of the cell membrane (p. 122).
quiz_exm1:23.alt: Photograph of a person at a console beside a large metal vacuum chamber with a round window

quiz_exm1:24.q: After fixation and dehydration, which two pieces of equipment does the lecture show for preparing a specimen for SEM?
quiz_exm1:24.r: SEM preparation: fixation in formalin, dehydration in ethanol (p. 124), then the critical point drying apparatus (p. 125) and the sputter coating unit with gold (p. 126).

quiz_exm1:25.q: Freeze-fracturing split the plasma membranes of two adjacent cells to give this view. What are the two exposed faces at X and Y called?
quiz_exm1:25.r: Freeze-fracturing exposes the E and P faces of the cell membrane (p. 122). Here the fracture plane crossed from one cell to the next, exposing the P-face and the E-face (p. 123).
quiz_exm1:25.alt: Grey textured micrograph divided by a dark jagged line into a left region marked X and a right region marked Y

quiz_exm1:26.q: Two immunohistochemistry methods are drawn. Which method is panel B, and what does the lecture say it does?
quiz_exm1:26.r: In panel B a second, labelled antibody binds the primary antibody: indirect immunohistochemistry, which amplifies the signal from the primary antibody (p. 106).
quiz_exm1:26.alt: Two drawings, A and B. In A one Y-shaped antibody sits on a green ball and carries an orange ball. In B a second Y-shaped antibody sits on the first and carries the orange ball

quiz_exm1:27.q: In immunohistochemistry the antibody is conjugated to a detectable label. Which examples of labels does the lecture give?
quiz_exm1:27.r: The primary or secondary antibody is conjugated to a detectable label, for example an enzyme or a fluorophore (p. 106).

quiz_exm1:28.q: Brown reaction product marks prostate specific antigen in this section. Where in the luminal cells is it, and how was it made visible?
quiz_exm1:28.r: The slide shows immunohistochemical staining of prostate specific antigen in the cytoplasm of prostate luminal cells with a chromogenic substrate (p. 107).
quiz_exm1:28.alt: Section of glands with brown-stained cells around open spaces, on a pale blue background

quiz_exm1:29.q: A pathologist wants to demonstrate reticular fibers. Which stain on the lecture's list does this, and what else does it show?
quiz_exm1:29.r: Silver stains the Golgi apparatus and reticular fibers (p. 103).

quiz_exm1:3.q: In the lecture's drawing of the light microscope, what is the part at the arrow, where the beam from the illuminator turns upward?
quiz_exm1:3.r: The mirror sits in the base next to the illuminator and turns the light up toward the condenser and specimen; the prism is at the top, where the light turns toward the eyepiece (p. 91).
quiz_exm1:3.alt: Drawing of a light microscope with a yellow light path and all labels removed; a yellow arrow points to a part in the base

quiz_exm1:30.q: Two stains on the lecture's list both demonstrate elastic fibers. Which pair is it?
quiz_exm1:30.r: Aldehyde fuchsin stains elastic fibers, and orcein stains elastic fibers, collagen fibers and cytoplasm as a counterstain (p. 103). Orcein is the most common elastic stain (p. 963).

quiz_exm1:31.q: In a section stained with hematoxylin and eosin, what does each dye stain according to the lecture's list?
quiz_exm1:31.r: Hematoxylin stains the nucleus and eosin the cytoplasm (p. 103).

quiz_exm1:32.q: A liver biopsy is stained to demonstrate stored glycogen. Which stain on the lecture's list is used?
quiz_exm1:32.r: Periodic Acid Schiff stains glycogen and glycoproteins (p. 103). It is also the stain that shows the basement membrane by light microscopy (p. 130).

quiz_exm1:33.q: Besides elastic fibers, what does orcein stain on the lecture's list?
quiz_exm1:33.r: Orcein: elastic fibers, collagen fibers and a cytoplasmic counterstain (p. 103).

quiz_exm1:34.q: On the lecture's slides for light microscopy, which step comes between dehydration and sectioning?
quiz_exm1:34.r: Light microscopy: fixation and dehydration (p. 97), embedding in paraffin (p. 98), sectioning with the microtome (p. 99), then mounting and staining (p. 100). Polymerization of the embedding medium belongs to the TEM sequence (p. 111).

quiz_exm1:4.q: What is the arrowed part of this light microscope, which sits directly above the specimen slide?
quiz_exm1:4.r: The objective lenses are mounted just above the specimen slide; the condenser lies below the stage (p. 91).
quiz_exm1:4.alt: Drawing of a light microscope with a yellow light path and all labels removed; a yellow arrow points to a part just above the stage

quiz_exm1:5.q: In the TEM, magnets focus the beam of electrons. According to the slide titles, which part does this focusing job in the light microscope?
quiz_exm1:5.r: The slide titles set the two side by side: 'Light Microscope (glass lens focus light)' (p. 91) and 'Transmission Electron Microscope (magnets focus a beam of electrons)' (p. 92).

quiz_exm1:6.q: In this drawing of the transmission electron microscope, what is the arrowed part at the foot of the column, just above the photographic film?
quiz_exm1:6.r: At the bottom of the TEM column the drawing stacks the fluorescent screen, the photographic film and the CCD camera (p. 92).
quiz_exm1:6.alt: Cutaway drawing of an electron microscope column with labels removed; a yellow arrow points to a flat plate at the bottom of the beam

quiz_exm1:7.q: The arrow marks the lowest lens in this transmission electron microscope, the last one before the screen. Which lens is it?
quiz_exm1:7.r: From top to bottom the TEM drawing shows the condenser lens (with its electric coil), the objective lens just under the specimen, the intermediate lens and the projector lens (p. 92).
quiz_exm1:7.alt: Cutaway drawing of an electron microscope column with labels removed; a yellow arrow points to the lowest ring-shaped part

quiz_exm1:8.q: The arrowed part appears in the lecture's drawing of the scanning electron microscope but not in its drawing of the TEM. What is it?
quiz_exm1:8.r: Both drawings share the cathode, anode, electron gun, electric coil and column. The scanner, the detector of electrons, the signal amplifier and the monitor are only on the SEM drawing (p. 93).
quiz_exm1:8.alt: Cutaway drawing of an electron microscope column with labels removed; a yellow arrow points to a small box attached to the side of the column

quiz_exm1:9.q: In this scanning electron microscope, the arrowed part sits beside the specimen and feeds the signal amplifier and monitor. What is it?
quiz_exm1:9.r: In the SEM drawing the detector of electrons sits next to the specimen and passes its signal to the signal amplifier and the monitor (p. 93). The fluorescent screen, projector lens and copper grid belong to the TEM drawing (p. 92).
quiz_exm1:9.alt: Cutaway drawing of an electron microscope column with labels removed; a yellow arrow points to a box beside the disc at the bottom

brief:
Microscopes and Stains (Examinus)

Everything here is from the Histologic Techniques slides, pp. 91–128. Page numbers are pages of the combined PDF.

1. The three microscopes

Light microscope (LM) Transmission electron microscope (TEM) Scanning electron microscope (SEM) Page
What focuses the beam Glass lenses focus light Magnets focus a beam of electrons Lenses with an electric coil 91–93
Top magnification 1,500 times 500,000 times 100,000 times 91–93
What the picture looks like Colour section Grey thin slice, detail inside cells Grey 3-D surface 94–96

2. Preparing the specimen

Step LM TEM SEM Page
Fixation Formalin Formalin, glutaraldehyde, osmium tetroxide Formalin 97, 109, 124
Dehydration Ethanol, xylene Ethanol Ethanol 97, 109, 124
Embedding Paraffin Epon, then polymerization None 98, 110–111
Cutting Microtome Diamond knife; ultrathin sections float in a boat of water None 99, 114–115
Support Glass slide Copper grid, 3 mm Metal stub 101, 116
Stain or coat Mounting and staining Lead citrate, uranyl acetate Critical point drying, then gold sputter coating 100, 117, 125–126

3. Parts on the drawings

Microscope Parts, in the order the beam meets them Page
LM Illuminator, mirror, light filter, condenser, specimen slide on the stage, objective lenses, prism, eyepiece 91
TEM Electron gun (cathode, anode), condenser lens with electric coil, specimen holder with copper grid, objective lens, intermediate lens, projector lens, fluorescent screen, photographic film, CCD camera 92
SEM Electron gun (cathode, anode), lenses with electric coil, scanner, specimen at the bottom, detector of electrons, signal amplifier, monitor 93

Only the SEM drawing has a scanner, a detector and a monitor. Only the TEM drawing has a fluorescent screen and a copper grid.

4. Freeze-fracture

Item Fact Page
Unit Balzers unit 121
What it exposes The E and P faces of the cell membrane 122–123

5. Stains for light microscopy

Stain What it shows Page
Hematoxylin Nucleus 103
Eosin Cytoplasm 103
Periodic Acid Schiff Glycogen, glycoproteins; the basement membrane 103, 130
Aldehyde fuchsin Elastic fibers 103
Orcein Elastic fibers, collagen fibers, cytoplasmic counterstain; the most common elastic stain 103, 963
Silver Golgi apparatus, reticular fibers 103

6. Immunohistochemistry

Item Fact Page
What it does Antibodies show where a specific antigen protein is in cells 106
Label Conjugated to the primary or secondary antibody: an enzyme or a fluorophore 106
Direct The primary antibody carries the label 106
Indirect A labelled secondary antibody binds the primary; amplifies the signal 106
Example Prostate specific antigen in the cytoplasm of prostate luminal cells, chromogenic substrate 107
